audits.title: Radiotherapy Dosimetry Audits in Taiwan Hospitals
audits.standard: Standards for Medical Exposure Quality Assurance (SMEQA) acceptance criteria
audits.setting: About 81 radiation therapy departments

cycle1.result: Over 78% of photon and 75% of electron beams within 1.0% of reference-point dose; all measurements within SMEQA acceptance criteria.

audits.other_findings: Over 300 photon and 400 electron beams measured each year; about 1.20 medical physicists per unit.
audits.citation: Shiau A, Hsu S, Huang P, Chen C, Huang Y, Lien K, et al.. Radiotherapy Dosimetry Audits in Taiwan Hospitals. . 2020. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-107292/v1.

audits.title: The 1998 Australian external beam radiotherapy survey and IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audit.
audits.standard: IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audit; combined standard uncertainty 1.8%
audits.setting: All Australian external beam radiotherapy centres

cycle1.result: Dose quoted by centres was in nearly every case within 1.5% of the IAEA-assessed dose.

audits.other_findings: Mean age of linear accelerators 7.1 years; other machines 14.7 years.
audits.citation: Huntley R, Izewska J. The 1998 Australian external beam radiotherapy survey and IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audit. Australas Phys Eng Sci Med. 2000;23(1):21-29. PMID: 10921198.

audits.title: The IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audits for radiotherapy: a perspective of dosimetry practices at hospitals in developing countries.
audits.standard: 5% acceptance limit for TLD dose
audits.setting: Hospitals in the IAEA/WHO TLD postal audit programme, mainly developing countries

cycle1.result: 84% of participants within the 5% acceptance limit.

audits.other_findings: Results poorer in hospitals not returning dosimetry data; under 10% used absorbed-dose-to-water codes.
audits.citation: Izewska J, Andreo P, Vatnitsky S, Shortt KR. The IAEA/WHO TLD postal dose quality audits for radiotherapy: a perspective of dosimetry practices at hospitals in developing countries. Radiother Oncol. 2003;69(1):91-97. doi:10.1016/s0167-8140(03)00245-7. PMID: 14597361.

audits.title: Postal dose audits for radiotherapy centers in Latin America and the Caribbean: trends in 1969-2003.
audits.standard: not reported
audits.setting: Radiotherapy centres in Latin America and the Caribbean (IAEA/WHO postal TLD audits)

cycle1.result: About 5,200 photon beams in over 1,300 centres checked; 36% in Latin America and the Caribbean, with results improving over the years.

audits.intervention: Follow-up programme for centres with poor results.
audits.other_findings: Centres without qualified medical physicists or dosimetry equipment had poorer results.
audits.citation: Izewska J, Vatnitsky S, Shortt KR. Postal dose audits for radiotherapy centers in Latin America and the Caribbean: trends in 1969-2003. Rev Panam Salud Publica. 2006;20(2-3):161-172. doi:10.1590/s1020-49892006000800013. PMID: 17199911.

audits.title: Dosimetry quality audit of high energy photon beams in greek radiotherapy centers.
audits.standard: IAEA TRS 398 dosimetry code of practice; tolerance limits and +/-3% dose deviation
audits.setting: All 23 Greek radiotherapy centres (31 linacs, 13 Co-60 units)

cycle1.result: 28% of units exceeded the acceptance limit in at least one mechanical parameter; 61% of Co-60 units and 24% of linacs deviated beyond +/-3%.

audits.other_findings: 31% of Co-60 units and 7% of linacs deviated beyond +/-5%.
audits.citation: Hourdakis CJ, Boziari A. Dosimetry quality audit of high energy photon beams in greek radiotherapy centers. Radiother Oncol. 2008;87(1):132-141. doi:10.1016/j.radonc.2008.01.023. PMID: 18343514.

audits.title: Quality audit of radiotherapy with EORTC mailed in water TL-dosimetry.
audits.standard: Absorbed dose within acceptable variation (≤4%) of the stated 2 Gy
audits.setting: 22 radiotherapy institutes in EORTC Radiotherapy Group trials; mailed TL dosimetry evaluated in Gothenburg

cycle1.result: 89% of 178 photon beams within acceptable levels (≤4%); mean ratio 1.012, SD 0.025.

audits.other_findings: Sample is beams measured, not patients.
audits.citation: Hansson U, Johansson KA. Quality audit of radiotherapy with EORTC mailed in water TL-dosimetry. Radiother Oncol. 1991;20(3):191-196. doi:10.1016/0167-8140(91)90096-y. PMID: 1852910.

audits.title: Analysis of regional radiotherapy dosimetry audit data and recommendations for future audits.
audits.standard: Audit protocol dosimetric tolerances
audits.setting: South East Central regional radiotherapy audit group

cycle1.result: Apart from minor resolved systematic errors, all audit results within protocol tolerances.

audits.other_findings: Some evidence of improvement with newer codes of practice; recommends audits of new technologies such as image-guided radiotherapy.

audits.title: An analysis of the regulatory program of quality audits in radiotherapy in Brazil from 1995 to 2007.
audits.standard: IAEA dosimetry protocols TRS 277 and TRS 398; national radiological protection requirements
audits.setting: 195 radiotherapy facilities with high-energy photon beams

cycle1.result: Dose deviation within ±3% for 67.6% of Co-60 units and 79.6% of linear accelerators; above 5% in 13.9% of Co-60 and 10.8% of linac facilities.

audits.other_findings: No check source in 38% of facilities, inadequate training in 9%, and no individual dose registry in 6%.
audits.citation: de Paiva E, da Rosa LA, Brito RR, de Sá LV, Dovales AC, Batista DV, et al.. An analysis of the regulatory program of quality audits in radiotherapy in Brazil from 1995 to 2007. J Appl Clin Med Phys. 2011;12(2):3330. doi:10.1120/jacmp.v12i2.3330. PMID: 21587175.

audits.title: Validating dose rate calibration of radiotherapy photon beams through IAEA/WHO postal audit dosimetry service.
audits.standard: IAEA/WHO postal audit dosimetry service (agreement of stated dose with IAEA measurement)
audits.setting: Radiation Oncology Department, Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi

cycle1.result: Agreement between stated doses and IAEA results within 1% for the two 6 MV beams and within 2% for the 18 MV beam.

audits.standard: IAEA recommendations and agreement criteria for measured vs calculated doses
audits.setting: Three radiotherapy departments

cycle1.result: All test cases with advanced algorithms were within agreement criteria; larger deviations with simpler algorithms and higher beam energies.

audits.other_findings: A few errors in basic dosimetry data in treatment planning systems were found and corrected.

audits.title: Remote auditing of radiotherapy facilities using optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters.
audits.standard: Pass (optimal) within 2 SD (<=2.6%), fail beyond 3 SD (>3.9%) for OSLD audit
audits.setting: Australian Clinical Dosimetry Service, radiotherapy facilities

cycle1.result: TLD audit of 108 photon beams: mean deviation 0.0%, SD 1.8%; all Pass (Optimal Level).

audits.intervention: Replacement of TLD-based audit with optically stimulated luminescence dosimeter audit and tighter tolerances.

cycle2.result: OSLD audit of 162 photon beams: mean deviation -0.2%, SD 1.4%; 94% Pass (Optimal Level), 6% Pass (Action Level).

audits.other_findings: All Pass (Action Level) results were resolved with repeat OSLD audit or on-site ion chamber measurement.
audits.citation: Lye J, Dunn L, Kenny J, Lehmann J, Kron T, Oliver C, et al.. Remote auditing of radiotherapy facilities using optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters. Med Phys. 2014;41(3):032102. doi:10.1118/1.4865786. PMID: 24593737.

audits.title: A national dosimetry audit for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy in lung.
audits.standard: Planned and delivered dose agreement within ±3.0%
audits.setting: UK radiotherapy centres (national mail-based dosimetry audit)

cycle1.result: Mean measured versus calculated dose difference 0.4±1.4% (alanine) and 1.4±3.4% (film) excluding pencil-beam; 25/27 SABR plans within ±3.0%.

audits.other_findings: Pencil-beam algorithm differences were -6.1% and -12.9%; geometric accuracy was better for VMAT and Cyberknife than conformal techniques.
audits.citation: Distefano G, Lee J, Jafari S, Gouldstone C, Baker C, Mayles H, et al.. A national dosimetry audit for stereotactic ablative radiotherapy in lung. Radiother Oncol. 2017;122(3):406-410. doi:10.1016/j.radonc.2016.12.016. PMID: 28117079.

audits.title: Results of a multicentre dosimetry audit using a respiratory phantom within the EORTC LungTech trial.
audits.standard: EORTC 22113-08113 LungTech trial radiotherapy quality assurance protocol
audits.setting: Twelve radiotherapy centres in the EORTC LungTech trial

cycle1.result: Reference output dose median variation 0.5% [-1.1, +1.5]. Chamber vs planned dose median deviation 1.8% (7.5 mm static), 1.1% (12.5 mm static), 3.2% (dynamic). Film gamma median pass rates 92.0%, 96.2% and 71.0% (7.5 mm dynamic).

audits.other_findings: Dynamic irradiations had significantly lower gamma pass rates than the 12.5 mm static plan (p = 0.001); total monitor units correlated with results.
audits.citation: Lambrecht ML, Eaton DJ, Sonke JJ, Nestle U, Peulen H, Weber DC, et al.. Results of a multicentre dosimetry audit using a respiratory phantom within the EORTC LungTech trial. Radiother Oncol. 2019;138:106-113. doi:10.1016/j.radonc.2019.06.008. PMID: 31252291.

audits.title: Radiotherapy dosimetry audits carried out in Ireland at the request of the National Radiation Safety Committee in 2014 & 2017.
audits.standard: Requirement for clinical audit in medical radiological procedures; MD Anderson Dosimetry Laboratory credentialing (phantom irradiation)
audits.setting: 11 radiotherapy centres in Ireland

cycle1.result: 22 audits across 11 centres; mean MDADL vs institution PTV dose 0.999 ± 0.026; mean PTV gamma pass rate at 7%/4 mm 97% (lower 95% CI 90%). All centres satisfied the phantom irradiation component.

audits.other_findings: Significant difference between prostate and head and neck irradiations.
audits.citation: Bradley FL. Radiotherapy dosimetry audits carried out in Ireland at the request of the National Radiation Safety Committee in 2014 & 2017. Phys Med. 2019;65:94-98. doi:10.1016/j.ejmp.2019.08.002. PMID: 31442879.

audits.title: A multinational audit of small field output factors calculated by treatment planning systems used in radiotherapy.
audits.standard: Action limit ±3% for 2 × 2 cm² field and ±2% for other fields versus reference output factors
audits.setting: Radiotherapy centres in five countries (IAEA multinational group)

cycle1.result: 30% and 31% of calculated 2 × 2 cm² output factors exceeded the 3% action limit for 6 MV and higher than 6 MV beams; over 200 beams collected.

audits.other_findings: Treatment planning systems generally overestimated small field output factors, increasingly with smaller field size.
audits.citation: Lechner W, Wesolowska P, Azangwe G, Arib M, Alves VGL, Suming L, et al.. A multinational audit of small field output factors calculated by treatment planning systems used in radiotherapy. Phys Imaging Radiat Oncol. 2018;5:58-63. doi:10.1016/j.phro.2018.02.005. PMID: 33458370.

audits.title: Dosimetric end-to-end tests in a national audit of 3D conformal radiotherapy.
audits.standard: Pass Optimal Level within 3.3%; Pass Action Level within 5%; Out of Tolerance beyond 5%
audits.setting: Australian radiotherapy facilities (about 90%), onsite audit by the Australian Clinical Dosimetry Service

audits.title: 50 Years of the IAEA/WHO postal dose audit programme for radiotherapy: what can we learn from 13756 results?
audits.standard: Agreement between measured and stated dose within ±5%
audits.setting: Radiotherapy centres in low- and middle-income countries (IAEA/WHO postal dose audit programme)

cycle1.result: About 50% acceptable results in early years.

audits.other_findings: Machines over 20 years old had lower agreement; repeat participation and modern dosimetry protocols gave better results.

audits.setting: MD Anderson Radiation Quality Assurance Lab (IROC), over 2500 facilities worldwide
